analysis.title: GS Saboureault - Positioning Mondays Week 41
key_insights: Fundamental L/S funds are grossing up (gross leverage +3.3 pts to 209.5%) but still leaning bearish (net leverage -0.2 pts to 52.9%, 6th percentile 1-year).
GS desk sees Asset Managers finishing small net sellers on the week. The desk reads this as no offense from the fundamental community with indices at or near record highs.
OpenAI revenue headlines triggered a wave of selling in Semis/Tech. The desk reads this as an indication of where positioning is relatively fuller.
Info Tech was by far the most net sold US sector by hedge funds this week (-1.0 SD 1-year), driven by long and short sales, after being the most net bought US sector in 4 of the past 5 weeks.
Support from non-economic buyers is less obvious: CTAs are 'on target', buybacks have slowed, and the retail bid was more hesitant.
Sentiment bounced to Neutral on most gauges. The GS Sentiment Indicator is the exception at -0.7 (from -0.9), which the desk attributes to its inertia.
The desk sees no shortage of potential marginal buyers should the Oil and Rates overhangs recede.
Catalyst-heavy week ahead: banks report from Tuesday, ASML Wednesday, TSMC Thursday, US CPI Wednesday, PPI, Retail Sales, Philly Fed, and a Warsh speech at the IMF Thursday.
Global equities were net sold by hedge funds (-0.3 SD 1-year) as short sales outpaced long buys 1.3 to 1. All major regions except Europe were net sold, led by North America and EM Asia.

Europe saw risk-on hedge fund flows for the 3rd consecutive week, with new longs outpacing new shorts 1.2:1. Europe is overweight vs MSCI World by 2.41% (flat w/w) and North America is underweight at -17.39%.
Hedge funds net sold US Consumer Staples for a 3rd straight week (7 of the last 8), driven entirely by short sales.

The buyback desk expects an inflection in repurchase volumes as earnings season starts and corporates exit blackout about 1-2 days after their releases. About 10% are expected to be in an open window by the end of the week.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were by far the most net sellers of US Info Tech this week (-1.0 SD 1-year), and the desk flags Semi/Tech as where positioning may be fuller after the OpenAI revenue headlines.
Hedge funds net sold the US sector for a 3rd straight week (7 of the last 8), driven entirely by short sales.
These were the most net bought global sectors by hedge funds this week.

earnings_insights: Earnings season starts this week, led by major Financials (banks from Tuesday), with ASML on Wednesday and TSMC on Thursday.
Buyback desk: corporates remain in pre-earnings blackout, with about 10% expected to be in an open window by the end of the week.

risk_factors: Fundamental investors are uncomfortable with indices at or near record highs.

vol_and_positioning: HF overall book gross leverage +0.7 pts to 308.7% (60th percentile 1-year). Net leverage -1.5 pts to 75.9% (10th percentile). L/S ratio -1.2% to 1.652 (14th percentile).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage +3.3 pts to 209.5% (43rd percentile). Net leverage -0.2 pts to 52.9% (6th percentile).
Macro Products were net sold, driven by short sales. Single Stocks saw little net activity.
TMT (Info Tech + Comm Svcs) and Materials were the most net sold global sectors.

CTAs sold about $23bn of Global Equities over the past week, leaving length around $44bn (45th percentile). They are expected to be small sellers on a one-week horizon in a flat market, with modest buying on a one-month horizon.
S&P E-mini levels to watch for CTA flows: 7704 (short-term), 7493 (medium-term), 7012 (long-term).
EPFR global equity funds saw inflows of $12.4bn w/w (vs $15.8bn outflows the week before). US funds +$3.3bn, Europe +$0.2bn, Japan -$3.3bn.
Retail bid was volatile, with 2 of the lowest (still positive) imbalance days since the beginning of August.
Buyback desk flows were at 0.8x vs both 2025 and 2024 YTD ADTV. 10b5-1 plans were 86% of desk volume vs 14% discretionary, compared with 89%/11% the prior week.
CFTC: asset managers were small net buyers of S&P futures in the week ending September 29th.

tension_points.bull_case: There seems to be no shortage of potential marginal buyers should the Oil and Rates overhangs recede, with hedge fund net leverage in the 10th percentile and fundamental L/S net leverage in the 6th percentile.
tension_points.bear_case: Fundamentals are not playing offense with indices near record highs, asset managers were small net sellers, CTAs are on target, buybacks slowed and the retail bid was hesitant.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil and Rates overhangs not receding, or CPI on Wednesday disrupting the rates backdrop.
